title: Will FEWS NET classify any area of Sudan as experiencing Famine before 2027?
resolution_criteria: This question will resolve as **Yes** if, in any [FEWS NET](https://fews.net/east-africa/sudan) classification map with a "Reported" date after August 2026 and before January 2027 shows at least one area, urban settlement, or settlement of displaced populations in IPC Phase 5: Famine (with solid or reasonable evidence) for the current period.
fine_print: Areas marked Phase 4 with the "!" symbol (would likely be Phase 5 without assistance) will not count.
background:
Sudan has been in civil war between the Sudanese Armed Forces and the Rapid Support Forces since April 2023, producing what is widely regarded as the world's largest active displacement and one of its most severe hunger crises.  

[FEWS NET](https://fews.net/east-africa/sudan) (Famine Early Warning Systems Network) is a food security early warning system originally established by USAID in 1985, now run by a network of U.S. government and technical partner organizations. It monitors 30+ food-insecure countries and produces regular Outlooks using a scale of Phase 1 (Minimal) through Phase 5 (Catastrophe/Famine).

In 2025, FEWS NET's operations were disrupted by the dismantling of USAID and associated funding cuts, taking the network offline for a period before it resumed publishing.

FEWS NET's own narrative has fluctuated: its December 2025 Sudan update stated Famine (IPC Phase 5) was "expected to persist amid escalating conflict and tightening sieges," while its February and March 2026 updates stated that Famine *thresholds* were "no longer met" in previously affected areas, describing instead a "credible risk of Famine" in South Kordofan, North Kordofan, North Darfur, and parts of Greater Darfur; while still noting "Emergency outcomes with populations in Catastrophe are ongoing" in specific hotspots.

comments.author: DeRuina
comments.text: I think the key detail here is how FEWS NET actually handles malnutrition evidence. In its June 2026 Outlook it reported GAM of 52% in Um Baru and 34% in Kernoi, both far above the Famine threshold, yet still withheld a Phase 5 classification because food consumption data only showed moderate hunger. The August 2026 Update kept that line, mapping Phase 4 with households in Catastrophe and using "credible risk of Famine" language, which does not count for resolution. Every time FEWS NET has actually coloured an area Phase 5 in Sudan since 2024, a prolonged siege was the trigger, not a nutrition survey. Right now the corridors to Kadugli and Dilling are open again after the May relief, and the October harvest is starting. So I see this as a question about sieges, not malnutrition data. The reason it's not a near-zero for me is that last year's classifications came in exactly this September–December window, Dilling has already been re-besieged twice in 2026, and the RSF has since taken Um Baru — one closed corridor plus a new SMART survey is a plausible path. The October Outlook is the next real read.

comments.author: Russell-viper
DaiLothbrook
comments.text: I will use, intially, for this questions,  the Famine-classification probability from 35% to 45% because the latest [FEWS NET Sudan analysis ](\(https://fews.net/east-africa/sudan\))identifies credible risk across multiple areas, extremely severe malnutrition in some locations, badly delayed rainfall, rising food prices, and humanitarian coverage below one fifth of estimated need. I stop below 50% because the[ June outlook ](\(https://fews.net/east-africa/sudan/food-security-outlook/june-2026\))treats Famine as a conditional alternative scenario rather than the most likely outcome, and because household-level Catastrophe doesn't automatically satisfy the consumption, malnutrition, and mortality thresholds required to classify an entire area as Famine; evidence access and the timing of formal publication add further resolution uncertainty in my view.

comments.author: A6N23
comments.text:
Poor agriculture season, conflict, displacement and constrained humanitarian funding drives the risk of famine in the mentioned areas.
Sept 14 (Reuters) - The World Food Programme's funding for Sudan — the world's largest hunger crisis — has fallen by about half this year. Last year, WFP received \$645 million, but almost three-quarters into this year funding is only at \$206 million.

Almost 20 million people face hunger in Sudan, but budget cuts have forced the WFP to focus efforts on the 5 million most in need, of whom it has recently scaled up to reach 4 million people.
Even then, the organisation, the UN's largest by budget, is forced to make difficult decisions.

comments.author: A6N23
comments.text:
**Sudan Food Security Outlook Update: Conflict and poor rains to drive Emergency and risk of Famine during harvest, August 2026 - January 2027**

There is a credible risk of Famine (IPC Phase 5) could occur through January in seven areas of northwestern and central North Darfur, and in Dilling and Kadugli of South Kordofan and nearby rural areas. Large to extreme food shortage are already widespread alongside high levels of malnutrition. If conflict escalates or severe sieges resume and isolate populations for a prolonged time in combination with marginal-to-no harvests, worsening food consumption deficits and hunger-related deaths combined with extreme acute malnutrition, then Famine (IPC Phase 5) would likely occur.

FEWS NET assesses a plausible risk of Famine (IPC Phase 5) in multiple areas of Sudan and South Sudan. All identified areas are already experiencing high levels of hunger and acute malnutrition, driven by years of conflict (which is considered the primary cause of food insecurity) and/or weather shocks.
